stanzas: 通りゃんせ 通りゃんせ
ここはどこの 細道じゃ
天神さまの 細道じゃ
ちっと通して 下しゃんせ
御用のないもの 通しゃせぬ
この子の七つの お祝いに
お札を納めに まいります
行きはよいよい 帰りはこわい
こわいながらも
通りゃんせ 通りゃんせ
orig.credit: Traditional; as quoted in Wikipedia's article (Japanese Wikipedia)

stanzas: Go through, go through.
Here, whose narrow path is this?
It is the narrow path of Tenjin-sama.
Please let us through a little.
Those who have no business here are not let through.
For the celebration of this child's seventh year
we are going to offer up a talisman.
Going is fine, fine; coming back is frightening.
Though it is frightening,
go through, go through.
Tōryanse tōryanse
koko wa doko no hosomichi ja
Tenjin-sama no hosomichi ja
chitto tōshite kudashanse
goyō no nai mono tōshasenu
kono ko no nanatsu no oiwai ni
ofuda o osame ni mairimasu
iki wa yoi yoi kaeri wa kowai
kowai nagara mo
tōryanse tōryanse

notes: lines 1 and 10: 'tōryanse' is an old Edo-period polite imperative, 'please pass through'.
line 2: literally 'here is the narrow path of where?'
line 3: Tenjin-sama is Sugawara no Michizane worshipped as a god, at a Tenmangū shrine.
line 6: the seventh year is the age of the Shichi-Go-San shrine visit, when a child was thought safely past early childhood.
line 7: the ofuda, a shrine talisman, is given back to the shrine in thanks.
line 8: why the way back is frightening is not said in the song; explanations differ.
